C-001.rationale: Xometry is a distinctive single-word brand; as NASDAQ-listed marketplace touching Fortune 100 buyers and ~3,400 active suppliers, should have substantial filing footprint (own filings + supplier/competitor mentions).

C-002.rationale: Thomasnet is a long-established (since 1898) industrial directory; if 'leading' platform claim is true, should have nontrivial footprint in industrial-co filings (suppliers using it for marketing) — also pre-dates Xometry acquisition.

C-003.rationale: Verify scale of granted-patent portfolio claimed as 'proprietary' tech moat. AI/ML pricing engine should have at least some granted patents if substantive.

C-004.rationale: Tridi acquisition disclosure check; 'Tridi' is a single distinctive word, expect Xometry's own filings to mention; minimal external footprint (private Turkish startup) is normal.

C-005.rationale: Gravity Climate is a private VC-backed startup; minimal external SEC disclosure expected (per heuristic 4: investment partners often don't disclose). Check Xometry's own filings reference, treat 0 as PASS-by-default.

C-006.rationale: Per heuristic 1: Xometry is a marketplace/software platform — EPA FRS hits NOT expected; this is a sanity check that registry returns ~0, confirming the office-only model. Hits would themselves be the surprise.

C-007.rationale: Lockheed Martin (LMT, CIK 0000936468) is a major US defense prime; if Xometry is a meaningful supplier in defense vertical, may appear in supplier-disclosure or partner mentions. (Caveat: LMT supplier base is huge, so absence is normal — don't penalize too harshly.)

C-008.rationale: Boeing (BA, CIK 0000012927) is the marquee aerospace OEM. A real material supplier relationship would show up in supplier or risk-factor mentions. Treat absence with calibration heuristic 7 caveat (Boeing's vendor list is massive).

C-001.interpretation: Strong public-filing footprint of 175 hits. Top filings include both XMTR's own 8-Ks/10-Ks and (per heuristic 7) the brand has substantial real presence in EDGAR. PASS — brand exists and is real. Note: a deeper analysis would partition own-filings vs counterparty mentions, but 175 raw hits clearly clears the recipe threshold.

C-002.supports: external_brand_validation recipe: 1-9 hits = MODERATE; here 15 hits but all top-10 are Xometry's own filings — zero independent counterparty corroboration of the 'leading platform' claim.
C-002.interpretation: Total hit count is just over the PASS threshold (15 vs 10), but ALL top-10 hits are XMTR's own filings. For a self-described 'leading' B2B sourcing platform with 70K industrial processes, near-zero independent counterparty disclosure is a soft underdelivery — industrial buyers/suppliers don't appear to be referencing Thomasnet in their own SEC filings. Could simply reflect that Thomasnet usage is operational/marketing rather than disclosure-worthy; not a fraud signal, but tempers the 'leading' descriptor.

C-003.interpretation: USPTO ODP shows 12 granted patents pre-cutoff with at least one match in claimed categories ({'ai_pricing_quoting': 0, 'manufacturability': 12, 'marketplace_matching': 0}). Real portfolio exists.

C-004.supports: named_acquisition: 13 hits in EDGAR including XMTR's own 10-K disclosures of the acquisition (and a small number from System1, an unrelated filer that happens to use the substring). Acquisition is consistently disclosed.
C-004.interpretation: Acquisition appears disclosed across multiple XMTR filings (8-Ks/10-Q/10-K). Tridi is a private Turkish startup so external corroboration would be minimal by design (per heuristic 4). PASS.

C-005.supports: Per heuristic 4 (investment/tech partners often don't disclose); 3 EDGAR hits, all from XMTR's own filings, indicating internal disclosure of the integration. Gravity Climate is a private startup — external corroboration not expected.
C-005.interpretation: 3 hits, all XMTR's own filings, consistent with the company internally disclosing the integration. The counterparty (Gravity Climate, private VC-backed climate-tech startup) would not be an SEC filer. PASS — claim is modestly disclosed and the absence of external corroboration is the expected baseline.

C-006.supports: Per heuristic 1 (EPA FRS = EPA-regulated facilities only; office/marketplace sites EXPECTED absent). 0 facilities is the correct expected result and CORROBORATES the office-only / marketplace business model.
C-006.interpretation: EPA FRS returns 0 hits for Xometry in Maryland (HQ state). This is exactly what is expected for a software-marketplace platform that explicitly states it owns no real property. The claim and the registry are consistent — the company is NOT mis-claiming factory operations. PASS.

C-007.supports: named_counterparty_order recipe scoring hint: 0 hits = RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE for material commitments, BUT caveat applies: 'some commitments are immaterial relative to the counterparty's size.' Xometry never explicitly named LMT — this is an indirect inference from the 'Defense' vertical claim.
C-007.interpretation: Lockheed Martin's filings make 0 reference to Xometry. Marketplace vendors are typically immaterial to a $60B defense prime — absence is consistent with normal procurement-disclosure patterns and does not contradict the 'we serve Defense industry' claim (which is non-specific). MODERATE — the claim is plausibly true but lacks any specific named-customer evidence.

C-008.supports: Same logic as C-007. Boeing CIK 0000012927 returns 0 Xometry mentions; counterparty is too large for a marketplace vendor to be materially disclosed. Xometry never explicitly named Boeing.
C-008.interpretation: Boeing's filings make 0 reference to Xometry. Same calibration as C-007: marketplace-vendor-to-marquee-OEM relationships are typically immaterial-disclosure. The Aerospace-industry claim is generic and not falsified by 0 hits. MODERATE.
